region: Burdett · Seneca Lake, Finger Lakes, New York
about: Ryan William Vineyard sits on Route 414 in Burdett, Schuyler County, on the east side of Seneca Lake, where the slopes face west across the deepest of the Finger Lakes. Founded and owned by Ryan Bossert, it is a working farm with its own vineyard, winery, tasting room and restaurant, the Tasting Barn, which serves farm-to-table food on a patio overlooking the lake. In August 2026 the winery won the Governor’s Cup, best wine of the New York Wine Classic, for its 2025 Pinot Blanc, an honour Bossert called “a decades long dream come true.”

Seneca Lake is so deep that it rarely freezes, and the stored warmth of its water softens spring frosts and lengthens autumn, giving the east shore one of the gentlest growing seasons in the region. That long, cool ripening keeps acidity bright in white grapes such as Chardonnay. This bottling carries the broader Finger Lakes appellation. Expect honeysuckle, kiwi and lime on the nose, apple and pineapple on the palate, and a creamy finish.
